q: What are the three borders of the posterior triangle of the neck?
options: Midline of the neck, anterior border of sternocleidomastoid, mandible
Posterior border of sternocleidomastoid, anterior border of trapezius, middle third of the clavicle
Both bellies of the digastric and the hyoid bone
Anterior border of trapezius, superior belly of omohyoid, first rib
why: In front: the back edge of sternocleidomastoid. Behind: the front edge of trapezius. Below: the middle third of the clavicle. Option A is the anterior triangle.

q: Which muscle splits the posterior triangle into the occipital and subclavian triangles?
options: Superior belly of omohyoid
Posterior belly of digastric
Inferior belly of omohyoid
Anterior scalene
why: The inferior belly of omohyoid crosses the lower part of the triangle. Above it is the big occipital triangle, below it the small subclavian triangle.

q: After a lymph node biopsy in the posterior triangle, a patient cannot shrug the shoulder on that side. Which nerve was injured?
options: Phrenic nerve
Accessory nerve (CN XI)
Suprascapular nerve
Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)
why: The accessory nerve runs superficially across the triangle, just under the investing fascia, on its way to trapezius. Cutting it weakens trapezius: the shoulder droops and shrugging is weak.

q: Why can a cut external jugular vein suck in air?
options: Because it carries arterial blood under high pressure
Because the investing fascia holds its wall open, and the pressure inside is lower than outside
Because it lies directly on the lung
Because it has no valves at all
why: Where the vein pierces the investing fascia, the fascia keeps it from collapsing. Breathing in creates negative pressure, so air can be drawn in (air embolism). Treatment: press on it immediately.

q: Where do you inject for a cervical plexus nerve block?
options: At the jugular notch
At the front edge of trapezius
At the posterior border of sternocleidomastoid, where its upper and middle thirds meet (the nerve point)
Just above the middle of the clavicle
why: The skin branches of the cervical plexus (C2–C4) come out together around the middle of the back edge of sternocleidomastoid – the nerve point of the neck.
